problem_statement: LangChain's tool-calling pipeline has accumulated a cluster of reliability and developer-experience gaps that make it hard to build robust, provider-agnostic tool-using agents. Developers injecting precomputed or programmatic tool-call history into agent workflows hit strict provider validation rules (such as Gemini's thought-signature and turn-order requirements) that reject otherwise valid message histories. When tool-call payloads arrive malformed or fragmented (bad function dicts, partially streamed arguments), the pipeline crashes or silently executes the wrong tool instead of degrading gracefully. Agents unconditionally force tool_choice='required', which breaks reasoning/thinking models that only support 'auto' or 'none'. Human-in-the-loop rejection flows are fragile: a tool call that a human rejects can still be executed by ToolNode because rejection enforcement is not reliably wired into execution. Observability is incomplete because tool_call_id is missing from on_tool_start (and reportedly on_tool_end) streaming events, making it impossible to attribute streamed output to a specific tool call when multiple tool calls run in parallel. Tool-call limits are enforced only after the fact, so agents waste calls and behave abruptly once a limit is hit with no prior warning. Finally, tool-level exception handling is inconsistent: ToolException raised inside wrap_tool_call middleware is not caught properly at the agent level, and handle_tool_error behaves differently between the @tool decorator and ToolNode, forcing developers to write workarounds. Together these gaps mean agent builders cannot fully trust that tool calls will be validated, executed, observed, limited, and error-handled consistently across providers and model types.
target_user: Developers building and operating LLM agents on LangChain who integrate tool-calling across multiple model providers, including those who inject programmatic tool-call history, use reasoning/thinking models, require human-in-the-loop approval, or run parallel tool calls in production.

user_stories.persona: an agent developer integrating with a strict-validation provider like Gemini
user_stories.action: inject precomputed tool-call messages into the conversation history without violating provider-specific turn-order or thought-signature rules
user_stories.value: I can build programmatic agent workflows that work across providers without hand-tuning message formats

user_stories.persona: an agent developer whose LLM streams tool-call arguments
user_stories.action: have malformed or partially streamed tool-call payloads detected and handled gracefully instead of crashing or silently executing incorrect tool calls
user_stories.value: my agent stays available and doesn't take unintended actions on bad input

user_stories.persona: a developer using a reasoning/thinking model
user_stories.action: have the agent select a tool_choice value the model actually supports instead of forcing 'required'
user_stories.value: my agent works with reasoning models without erroring out or requiring manual overrides

user_stories.persona: a developer building a human-in-the-loop approval flow
user_stories.action: trust that a rejected tool call is never executed by ToolNode
user_stories.value: I can safely gate sensitive tool actions behind human approval

user_stories.persona: a developer debugging an agent that runs tool calls in parallel
user_stories.action: see tool_call_id included on on_tool_start and on_tool_end streaming events
user_stories.value: I can attribute streamed events to the correct tool call and debug parallel execution accurately

user_stories.persona: a developer running agents with a bounded tool-call budget
user_stories.action: receive a proactive warning as the tool-call limit approaches rather than only learning after it's hit
user_stories.value: my agent can wrap up gracefully instead of behaving abruptly when the limit is reached

user_stories.persona: an agent developer handling tool errors
user_stories.action: have ToolException from wrap_tool_call middleware caught consistently at the agent level, with handle_tool_error behaving the same way across @tool and ToolNode
user_stories.value: I can write one error-handling strategy instead of separate workarounds for each code path

acceptance_criteria.given: a precomputed tool-call message history is injected for a provider with strict turn-order/thought-signature validation
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent sends the history to the provider
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is accepted without validation errors caused solely by injected message ordering or missing signatures

acceptance_criteria.given: a streamed tool-call payload arrives malformed or only partially complete
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent attempts to parse and execute it
acceptance_criteria.then: the agent does not crash and does not execute the tool with incorrect arguments, instead surfacing a recoverable error or skipping execution

acceptance_criteria.given: the active model only supports tool_choice values of 'auto' or 'none'
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent configures the tool-calling request
acceptance_criteria.then: the agent does not send tool_choice='required' and instead uses a supported value

acceptance_criteria.given: a human reviewer rejects a proposed tool call in a human-in-the-loop flow
acceptance_criteria.then: the tool is not executed and the rejection is recorded in the conversation state

acceptance_criteria.given: two or more tool calls are executed in parallel
acceptance_criteria.when: on_tool_start and on_tool_end events are emitted
acceptance_criteria.then: each event includes the tool_call_id matching the originating tool call

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent is approaching its configured tool-call limit
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent has one call remaining before the limit
acceptance_criteria.then: the agent emits a proactive warning signal before the limit-triggered behavior occurs

acceptance_criteria.given: a tool raises ToolException inside wrap_tool_call middleware
acceptance_criteria.when: the exception propagates to the agent level
acceptance_criteria.then: the agent catches it and applies the configured handle_tool_error behavior identically whether the tool was defined via @tool or invoked through ToolNode

success_metrics.name: provider validation failures
success_metrics.definition: count of reported issues where injected tool-call history fails strict provider validation (e.g., Gemini turn-order/thought-signature errors)
success_metrics.target: zero recurrences of the reported case within two release cycles

success_metrics.name: malformed payload crash rate
success_metrics.definition: count of crash or silent-incorrect-execution reports tied to malformed or fragmented streamed tool-call payloads
success_metrics.target: reduce from 2 known reports to 0 within two release cycles

success_metrics.name: rejected tool call execution incidents
success_metrics.definition: count of reported cases where a human-rejected tool call was executed by ToolNode

success_metrics.name: tool_call_id observability coverage
success_metrics.definition: proportion of tool streaming event types (on_tool_start, on_tool_end) that include tool_call_id in their payload, measured out of 2 target event types

success_metrics.name: tool error handling consistency
success_metrics.definition: count of distinct code paths (@tool decorator, ToolNode, wrap_tool_call middleware) with divergent handle_tool_error/ToolException behavior
success_metrics.target: reduce from the current 2+ divergent paths to 1 unified behavior

out_of_scope: Adding support for new LLM providers beyond fixing compatibility with existing strict-validation providers
Building a new UI for human-in-the-loop tool approval workflows
Redesigning the overall agent orchestration/state-machine architecture
Performance optimization of tool execution latency
Adding new built-in tools or tool libraries

risks.description: Each pain point in this theme has a frequency of only 1 or 2 reported issues, so the evidence base per individual sub-problem is thin; prioritization across these seven fixes is based on limited signal rather than broad usage data.
Hardening message-history validation for one strict provider (e.g., Gemini) risks introducing regressions or special-casing that complicates behavior for other providers.
Changing tool_choice defaults for reasoning models could alter existing agent behavior for users who rely on the current forced 'required' setting, causing silent behavior changes.
Human-in-the-loop rejection enforcement touches safety-critical paths; an incomplete fix could give developers false confidence that rejected calls are blocked when edge cases remain unhandled.
Unifying handle_tool_error semantics across @tool and ToolNode may be a breaking change for existing agents that depend on the current divergent behavior.
